source_text: Περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν ἐπισυνάπτειν ἐν ταῖς συνάξεσι τοὺς ψαλμούς, ἀλλὰ διὰ μέσου καθ᾽ ἕκαοτον ψαλμὸν γίνεσθαι ἀνάγνωσιν.
thought_title: Psalms must be separated by readings
orientation: The Council of Laodicea is issuing its own decrees, and this canon regulates how psalms are to be performed in the assemblies.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the not needing to join together the psalms in the assemblies, but through the middle after each psalm a reading is to take place.

choices.why: The verb means to connect or attach one thing to another; the canon forbids running psalms back-to-back without interruption.
The term refers to the gathered liturgical assembly of the church, matching the council's liturgical context.
The phrase indicates an intervening element between the psalms, preserving the spatial metaphor of the Greek.

choices.english: a reading is to take place
choices.why: The infinitive with δεῖν carries the force of obligation; the reading is the required intervening element.

pass_b_english: Psalms are not to be joined together one after another in the assemblies. Instead, a reading is to take place through the middle, after each psalm.
notes: The source has ἕκαοτον, an apparent misspelling for ἕκαστον (each).
